gloss: to carry in; to bring in; to haul into

definitions.gloss: to carry in; to bring in; to haul into a place
definitions.explanation: To move something bulky or heavy into a building or enclosed space. The compound stresses the endpoint of the movement: the object ends up inside.

examples.japanese: {荷物|にもつ}を{運|はこ}び{込|こ}んだ。
けが{人|にん}が{病院|びょういん}に{運|はこ}び{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: The injured person was rushed into the hospital.

examples.japanese: {業者|ぎょうしゃ}が{朝早|あさはや}くから{機材|きざい}を{会場|かいじょう}に{運|はこ}び{込|こ}んでいた。
examples.english: The contractors had been hauling equipment into the venue since early morning.

notes:
Compound of {運|はこ}ぶ (to carry) + {込|こ}む (into). Transitive: the thing carried takes を and the destination takes に.

ASPECT (ている):
{運|はこ}び{込|こ}んでいる can mean either an action in progress (is carrying things in) or a resulting state (has brought them in and they are there); context decides.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {病院|びょういん}に{運|はこ}び{込|こ}まれる: to be rushed to hospital
- {荷物|にもつ}を{部屋|へや}に{運|はこ}び{込|こ}む: to carry luggage into a room
- {機材|きざい}を{運|はこ}び{込|こ}む: to haul in equipment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {持|も}ち{込|こ}む: to bring in — smaller items carried by hand, often where permission is at issue
- {搬入|はんにゅう}する: to deliver in — formal, used of freight and exhibition setup
